function: Near-field channel estimation: a conditional diffusion model refines the SOMP initial estimate of the uplink XL-MIMO channel, with a non-Markovian sampler for speed (p. 4-8).
system: Uplink XL-MIMO OFDM, BS ULA with 256 antennas, 16 RF chains, 16 single-antenna users, 28 GHz, 100 MHz, 256 subcarriers, near-field spherical wavefront, no RIS (p. 3, 10).
method: Conditional diffusion model (NM-GDM), PixelCNN++/U-Net backbone with ResNet+ and attention blocks, trained offline to predict noise from (SOMP estimate, true channel) pairs; Adam; 100 sampling steps (p. 6-11).
data_channel: Custom simulated spherical-wavefront near-field channel following [15], L=6 paths; 70,000 pairs of SOMP estimate and true channel, split 5:1:1 for training, validation, test (p. 4, 10-11).
test_conditions: Tested at SNR -10 to 20 dB, users at 15-25 m and 350-400 m, pilot lengths 32 and 8, varied antennas; training distances and antennas not stated (p. 10-14).
baselines: Non-learned: polar-domain SOMP and SIGW, angular-domain SW-OMP and SS-SIGW-OLS, LS, genie-aided LS bound; learned: CNN-based L-DAMP [33] (p. 12-14).
metrics: NMSE versus SNR, pilot length, number of antennas and distance; training loss; sampling steps; parameters and GFLOPs (p. 11-14).
complexity: Stage 1 O(L Q N_RF S K); denoising network 7.82 GFLOPs and 11.82 million parameters; NM-GDM about 10 times faster sampling than GDM (p. 11-12).
q1_support: p. 10: "H is generated following the method in [15] to ensure a" - own spherical-wavefront simulator (Eq. 1, p. 4) with L=6 paths; no 3GPP model and no measured data.
q2_support: p. 11: "validation, and testing sets are divided in a 5 : 1 : 1 ratio."; p. 13: "the NM-GDM is also robust in the FF region, where users" - the paper claims robustness for far-field distances, other antenna counts and pilot lengths, but never states the training distances, antenna count or pilot length, so no test outside the training conditions is stated.
q3_support: p. 12: "L-DAMP [33], the polar-domain SOMP [15] and SIGW"; p. 13: "Fig. 8(a) presents the NMSE of our algorithm and the"
q4_support: p. 12: "proposed model, resulting in 7.82 GFLOPs and 11.82 million"
q5_support: p. 10: "we generate the corresponding channel data pairs" - data come from the authors' own simulator; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset.
notes: Included, area 2 (channel estimation, refinement of an initial compressed-sensing estimate). q1 is 0: the channel is a custom spherical-wavefront simulator following Cui and Dai [15] (p. 4, 10). q2 is 0 because the paper states no train/test mismatch: Table I and Section V-A give no training distance range, antenna count or pilot length, while Figs. 8-11 vary SNR, distance, antennas and pilots (p. 13-14); the abstract claims generalization in near- and far-field regions. If the reviewer can show from the figures that one model was tested outside its training conditions, q2 could be 1. q3: L-DAMP [33] is an earlier learned estimator compared on NMSE with non-learned SOMP, SIGW, SW-OMP, SS-SIGW-OLS and LS (Figs. 8-11, p. 12-14); polar-domain SOMP is the first stage of the method, so it is an ablation and not counted as the learned baseline. q4: 7.82 GFLOPs and 11.82 million parameters (p. 12) and O(L Q N_RF S K) for stage 1 (p. 11). q5 is 0: no link, no public dataset (p. 10-11).
